messages:
Maria: Fwd from ACME - they want to run a short Dedicated POC but they have two network requirements: IPv6 egress from our endpoint and mutual TLS (mTLS) client cert auth to their firewall. Can we actually do both for a POC without a full Private/VPC install?
Jason: We can support mTLS but with caveats. Hosted Dedicated pools (our managed infra) don't terminate customer client certs today. mTLS termination is supported on Private deployments (customer VPC or on-prem).
Sophia: IPv6 egress is tricky — most of our Dedicated pools are IPv4-only right now. We do have a couple of customers on a dual-stack experiment but not enabled by default.
Maria: Ok — ACME wants a quick test this week. They can't open more infra on their side yet. What are the practical options to unblock the POC?
Jason: Options: 1) Temporary hosted API key + CIDR allowlist (IPv4 only) to validate functionality. 2) Quick Private sandbox (short-lived) where we deploy a Private control plane in their VPC — supports mTLS and native IPv6 if their VPC/network team enables it. 3) Use a TLS passthrough/proxy in their network that terminates client certs and forwards to our endpoint (we'd still see source IPv4).
Tim: From security side: mTLS is preferred for high-assurance traffic. If they do a proxy we need the network diagram and that proxy must preserve client identity headers or present a signed token. Also need their security questionnaire answers for data flow and cert rotation.
Maria: They asked about pricing for the Private sandbox — ballpark for a week?
Jason: For a one-week Private POC we typically do a time-limited evaluation contract: minimal platform fee + reserved capacity for the test. I can draft a PO. If it's just to validate mTLS we can often do a no-cost lab deployment for partners, but IPv6 adds infra ops — may need a small pass-through fee.
Sophia: If they go Private we can enable mutual TLS at the ingress LB. Example nginx snippet we use for testing:```
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  ssl_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/server.crt;
  ssl_certificate_key /etc/ssl/private/server.key;
  ssl_client_certificate /etc/ssl/certs/ca.crt;
  ssl_verify_client on;
  location / {
    proxy_pass https://upstream;
  }
}```
Maria: Nice. They also asked whether we can provide a static egress IP for allowlisting while they sort IPv6.
Sophia: Yes — we can allocate a static NAT egress IP for Dedicated POCs. It will be IPv4. We'll provide the IPs and expected maintenance window (usually none during a one-week POC).
Maria: What info do you need from ACME right now to move forward?
Tim: Network diagram (simple), CIDR ranges they want allowed, if they will present client certs from a proxy or direct, and the completed security questionnaire (I can send the doc). Also contact for cert rotation if using mTLS.
Jason: I'll propose a two-track POC: Track A (fast): Hosted dedicated pool + static IPv4 egress + API key for functional tests. Track B (full): Private sandbox with mTLS + IPv6 (if their VPC supports it). We can flip to B if A shows blockers.
Maria: I'll ask them which track they'd prefer. Can we give them a curl example they can run if they do the proxy approach?
Sophia: Yep, sample curl for a proxy that presents client certs to the firewall (they'd replace cert paths):
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  --cert /path/to/client.crt \
  --key /path/to/client.key \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD-TEST-KEY" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Maria: Perfect. I'll get them the checklist.
deploy-bot: provisioning:dedi-poc-1785 started (ETA ~ 6h) :rocket:
Jason: Nice — that's the templated Dedicated sandbox. If that finishes we can hand over the static egress IP and a temporary API key for them to test while we finalize mTLS/Private options.
Maria: Thanks all — I'll update ACME and loop back with their answer before EOD tomorrow.
